messages:
jensen_customer: Hey @alex_support — our March invoice spiked ~23% vs the usage dashboard. We use streaming SSE (chunked partial gens) and I suspect reconnects are inflating tokens. Example session: sess_8HkLqZ. Ledger ref ASN-4821. Can someone investigate?

alex_support: Thanks Jensen — sorry about the surprise. Can you paste the raw SSE frames/transcript and a request_id or span id? We'll pull ledger events. Pinging @ingrid_engineer and @sam_billing.

ingrid_engineer: From similar incidents, the usual suspect is multiple finalize events across a reconnect + missing idempotency on the ledger commit. If both old socket and resumed socket call finalize, the ledger can double-apply token counts. Paste the exact frames and timestamps if you can.

jensen_customer: here's a scrubbed transcript (timestamps removed):
```
event: chunk
data: {"req_id":"r-9a1","tokens":64}

event: heartbeat
data: {}

event: chunk
data: {"req_id":"r-9a1","tokens":48}

event: finalize
data: {"req_id":"r-9a1","final":true}

# client reconnects (resume=true)
event: open
data: {"session":"sess_8HkLqZ","resume":true}

event: chunk
data: {"req_id":"r-9a1","tokens":32}

event: finalize
data: {"req_id":"r-9a1","final":true}
```
Note the finalize appears twice after resume. Dashboard shows ~144 tokens; invoice charged ~288.

alex_support: Got it. That transcript helps a lot. @sam_billing can you confirm ledger shows two commits for r-9a1? Also cc @leo_sre to check if handoff created duplicate delivery.

sam_billing: Pulling ledger ASN-4821 now... I see two finalize commits for req r-9a1 at 3105557894 and 3105557902. Charges match the doubled token amount. We can issue a credit; opening BILL-1174 to track.

ingrid_engineer: Repro I ran locally (quick notes):
```bash
# open initial SSE connection
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?session=sess_local" &
# send partial generation events, then finalize
# simulate network disconnect, then reconnect and resume
# on reconnect server accepts resume and emits buffered chunks + sends finalize again
```
Root cause summary: finalize is emitted by connection teardown and again by the resumed consumer; ledger handler dedupe is by event GUID only, not by (session_id, req_id). Proposed fixes: 1) use session_id+req_id as ledger idempotency key; 2) server-side: ensure finalize is only written once per req_id regardless of connection; 3) short-term: treat duplicate finalize as non-billable and auto-credit.

alex_support: For immediate relief we'll credit the duplicate charges on ASN-4821 and mark BILL-1174 as P1. @jensen_customer — we'll need the invoice number DM'd to billing and I'll ask finance to expedite. Also, as a quick client-side mitigation try resume=false on reconnects and see if that stabilizes counts.

jensen_customer: DMed invoice 2026-03-07-4821. I ran a quick test with resume=false and counts matched the dashboard. Thanks for the quick triage.

leo_sre: Adding a note — there's also a rarer path where a heartbeat frame marked 'finalize_pending:true' was interpreted as finalize by a backend worker that had a delayed dedupe cache eviction. I added a trace on worker id=7 to watch finalize flow.

sam_billing: Credit applied; invoice updated. You should see corrected PDF in the billing console in ~10 minutes. Reference: BILL-1174/ASN-4821/credit-2026-03-07. :white_check_mark:

alex_support: Wrapping up action items: ING-859 (server idempotency key changes), SRE to roll tracing and validate worker dedupe cache, BILL-1174 for manual credit & monitoring, customer to verify invoice. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
